0.long_answer: Malignant rhabdoid tumors of the central nervous system, also known as atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumors (AT/RT), are highly aggressive tumors that are characterized by deletions or mutations in the INI1/hSNF5 gene located on chromosome 22. When these tumors occur in the posterior fossa, the region of the brain that includes the cerebellum and brainstem, they most commonly affect the cerebellum. More specifically, within the cerebellum, AT/RTs are frequently found in the cerebellar hemispheres rather than in the midline vermis. This distribution helps distinguish them from other posterior fossa tumors such as medulloblastomas, which typically arise in the cerebellar vermis.
